34.s: Dolphin Street address and telephone are given and Pasley points the interviewer to Alton Purnell.
34.q: Yeah. Yeah. Sixty-eight-tee, what did you call it? Sixty-eighteen Dolphin. Sixty-eighteen Dolphin. Sixty-eighteen Dolphin. Sixty-eighteen Dolphin. Sixty-eighteen Dolphin.

34.t: Pencil and paper; Kid Punch still living
34.s: Writing materials; interviewer comments on many New Orleans musicians still in California.
34.q: Yeah. I can't call them all. Somebody said Punch is still living.

430.t: Where to find Walter Blue's wife and relatives
430.s: They discuss who could be asked about Walter Blue and where his relatives live.
430.q: She lived back in the firegrounds the last time or something. Oh, you know who could tell you? Yeah, Lawrence Morera.

474.t: Looking for a fellow musician and the neighborhood
474.s: Allen checks a name, they discuss the old neighborhood, St. Francis church and how to contact a musician.
474.ch: Donaldsonville, family and Richard M. Jones
474.q: In this neighborhood when I came here? Mm-hmm. When I came in this neighborhood there was a Catholic contractor right around there with that dollar there. Oh yeah? That's about all I know. And the Catholic Church is still there, St. Catholic. Was that a white church? At that time it was, but now…

1.t: Pianist sisters and a musician's illness
1.s: Barker and the interviewer try to work out the wives of two musicians, pianist sisters from across the lake, and one musician's sickness.
1.q: Chani Bebe's wife was a pianist. Yeah, her name was Crosby? Yeah, she had some sisters who played piano. Yeah. So I think there's a connection. I'm sure there's sisters. Yeah. D.D.'s wife and Chani Bebe's wife. Uh-huh. Or sisters. All the sisters played piano. They were from across the lake…

475.t: Celestin band members and their addresses
475.s: Russell asks for addresses of band members; French names Joe Thomas, Jeanette and Norwood Kimball, Steele Davis and Sidney Brown.
475.q: Well Norwood Kimball and I have still two, Steele Davis you see. Out of town I mean Norwood plays out of town job with me and Steele Davis plays a job at any time.

284.s: The interviewer asks for Joe Rena's or his wife's address.
284.q: No, I don't know Joe's address. I don't know his address. But, uh, I know his, I know Renee's wife's address and she might could tell you.

476.s: They ask whether a nice musician, now in California, came from Bay St. Louis.
476.q: Sure. Emmerdale Delahooza, is he from here? He's a nice little sight.

477.s: Wilson's daughter was named after Marian McPartland; they worked closely and were friends.
477.q: We worked a lot together. We were really very close.

110.t: Aside about Weatherwax's friend Georgia Frontiere
110.s: A side conversation about a wealthy supporter of the Brubeck Institute, with Gioia saying it will be edited out.
110.ch: Three D's and Bay Area struggles
110.q: When we play at Pepperdine, we usually stay in their Malibu [home], if it’s offered to us. I don’t know if we should say she owns 36 homes.

29.s: Howard says Belle is her last name; she was a friend of Susie's and a fine pianist.
29.ch: Union career, Masons, mentoring and the Clef Club
29.q: Sure. She's a friend of Susie's. Her last name was Belle.

413.s: Maxwell knew Jack Jenny's records and his wife Bonnie Lake, a friend of Artie's.
413.q: No, I didn't know very much about him at all. I have one or two of his records and I know his solos by heart, a couple beautiful tunes. And I knew the woman he was married to, Bonnie Lake I knew very well. She was a good friend of my brother-in-law's, Artie's. In fact, I still see her from time to…
